lines.text: You drove on. Their lights never came back.
lines.cap:
YOU DROVE ON. THEIR LIGHTS
NEVER CAME BACK.

lines.text: Day five. Your car has eleven miles left.
And the road is about to cost you the car.
lines.cap:
AND THE ROAD IS ABOUT TO
COST YOU THE CAR.

lines.text: Every road south ends here. A six-mile queue, for one bridge.
lines.cap:
ROADS SOUTH END HERE.
SIX MILES. ONE BRIDGE.

lines.text: Rule one. Walk the sleepers, never the ballast. Stone is loud.
So you leave the car on your terms. And you take the railway.
lines.cap:
YOU LEAVE ON YOUR TERMS.
AND TAKE THE RAILWAY.

lines.text: Radio. Recovery in six days. All rail staff evacuated on day one.
lines.cap:
RECOVERY IN SIX DAYS.
RAIL STAFF: GONE DAY 1.

lines.text: Rule two. Count bridges, not miles.
Eleven miles. Four bridges. A freight yard.
A locomotive. Idling. Nobody in the cab.
lines.cap:
A LOCOMOTIVE. IDLING.
NOBODY IN THE CAB.

lines.text: Rule three. Never shelter anywhere with one door.
Between you and the train: a signal box. One room. One door.
lines.cap:
BETWEEN YOU AND THE TRAIN:
A SIGNAL BOX. ONE DOOR.

lines.text: Four fifty-five. You go in for the yard keys.
lines.cap:
4:55 AM. YOU GO IN
FOR THE YARD KEYS.

lines.text: The staircase creaks. Behind you.
Driver? That you? I've held this train nine days, mate. Come down.
All rail staff evacuated on day one. The radio said so.
lines.cap:
RAIL STAFF: GONE DAY 1.
THE RADIO SAID SO.

lines.text: There is no driver.
Then the loop plays past where it ever has. The second half isn't a rescue.
lines.cap:
THEN THE LOOP PLAYS PAST
WHERE IT EVER HAS.

lines.text: It's a warning.
Do you go down the stairs?
